title: Sub-lemma D: isolate and prove the exact role of the hypothesis n >= 5 in the necessity (rigidity) step

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Issue.** The statement *requires* $n\ge5$. A complete proof must pinpoint precisely where $n\ge5$ is used (almost surely in the punctured-grid connectivity / rank-one rigidity step of Sub-lemma C) and must explain why smaller $n$ can fail (either the grid disconnects after deleting the diagonal, or the rigidity that forces product form collapses).

**What must be proved.** (i) For $n\ge5$ the relevant punctured fibers are connected / the rank-one rigidity holds; (ii) a sentence-level identification of the step that consumes $n\ge5$; ideally (iii) a small-$n$ obstruction showing the hypothesis is necessary.

**Failure mode to avoid.** A proof of necessity that never uses $n\ge5$ is almost certainly wrong.
